profile.headline: Software Engineer at Meta, AI Infra & Inference Platform | Stanford MS CS (AI)
profile.summary:
Software engineer on Meta's AI Infrastructure / Inference Platform team, focused on recommendation model debugging and agentic tooling. Over 5 years at Meta spanning AI infra and inference, plus Accounts Center product, privacy and data governance. 

Stanford MS in Computer Science with an AI specialization (NLP, deep learning, computer vision). Earlier: HCI research published at CHI and ASSETS, and founder of angstromCTF, a cybersecurity competition that has served thousands of high-school students.

Interested in LLM infrastructure, training/inference systems, and applied ML, as well as backend and distributed systems more broadly.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
AI Infra, Inference Platform (2025-present)
-Building new developer tools for debugging recommendation model inference reliability across Facebook, Instagram, and Ads ranking.

Cross-App Experiences & Privacy (earlier)
-Built privacy/data-governance infrastructure for cross-app linking data (compliant with global regulations) and led API migrations across thousands of call sites.
-Built UI and backend for Accounts Center, powering account linking and profile syncing/editing for 700M+ users across Facebook and Instagram.
positions.insights: Skills: PyTorch · Recommender Systems · Machine Learning

positions.title: Graduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Introduction to Human Computer Interaction Design (CS147 Autumn 2019), Computer Organization and Systems (CS107 Winter & Spring 2020)

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Worked on platform to crowdsource sidewalk accessibility data using Google Street View and assist people with disabilities in navigation. Implemented tools to interactively model and visualize crowdsourced accessibility data using various technologies including node.js, turf,
mapbox, and deck.gl.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Taught UNIX concepts as a TA in Introduction to Cybersecurity, a course in the ACES cybersecurity honors college. Responsibilities include developing course material, holding office hours, and delivering lecture content as needed.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description: Implemented new features in Facebook’s Android application to give users a greater level of control over the content they see. Contributed to a large existing codebase working with a variety of technologies including Java, GraphQL, Mockito, and numerous internal tools.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description: Developed newsfeed and notification-related features for Facebook Lite, an extremely data and space-efficient version of Facebook's mobile app with over 500 million users worldwide.

positions.title: Contest Organizer, angstromCTF
positions.description: Founded and led development of angstromCTF, a new cybersecurity competition for high school students. Successfully designed, implemented, and hardened scalable cloud server infrastructure used by over 800 competition participants. Contributed to development of competition submission and scoring framework written in Django Python.

honors.title: Banneker/Key Scholarship

honors.issuer: Issued by University of Maryland · Apr 2016

honors.title: National Merit Scholarship

honors.issuer: Issued by National Merit Scholarship Corporation · Apr 2016

projects.title: Brakedown - HopHacks 2016
projects.description: A real-time, collaborative browser-based driving game built using node.js and socket.io.

publications.title: Interactively Modeling and Visualizing Neighborhood Accessibility at Scale: An Initial Study of Washington DC
